Partial dependence of a model on one predictor

Source: R/helpers.R
partial_dependence.Rd

Sets one predictor to the same value in every row of the data, predicts, averages the predictions, and repeats for each value (Friedman, 2001). Plotted against the values, the result shows how the predictions change with the predictor, averaged over the other predictors. Used in Advanced Statistics for random forests from ranger, but it works with any model that has a predict() method.

Usage

partial_dependence(model, data, var, values, class = NULL)

Arguments

model

A fitted model. For a classification forest from ranger, fit it with probability = TRUE.

data

The data to predict for, usually the data the model was fitted to.

var

Name of the predictor, as a string.

values

Values of the predictor to set, such as seq(18, 80, by = 2). For a factor, levels of the factor.

class

For models that predict a probability for each class: the class whose probability to average, such as "deleted".

Value

A tibble with one row per value and the columns value and prediction, the mean prediction (or probability of class).

References

Friedman, J. H. (2001). Greedy function approximation: A gradient boosting machine. Annals of Statistics, 29(5), 1189–1232.

Examples

library(simling)
m <- lm(rt ~ log_freq * length, data = megastudy)
partial_dependence(m, megastudy, "length", 3:12)
#> # A tibble: 10 × 2
#>    value prediction
#>    <int>      <dbl>
#>  1     3       724.
#>  2     4       736.
#>  3     5       749.
#>  4     6       762.
#>  5     7       775.
#>  6     8       787.
#>  7     9       800.
#>  8    10       813.
#>  9    11       826.
#> 10    12       838.

if (requireNamespace("ranger", quietly = TRUE)) {
  rf <- ranger::ranger(deleted ~ following + morph + rate + age, data = td_deletion,
                       num.trees = 200, probability = TRUE, seed = 1)
  partial_dependence(rf, td_deletion, "age", seq(20, 80, by = 10), class = "deleted")
}
#> # A tibble: 7 × 2
#>   value prediction
#>   <dbl>      <dbl>
#> 1    20      0.671
#> 2    30      0.644
#> 3    40      0.680
#> 4    50      0.600
#> 5    60      0.514
#> 6    70      0.497
#> 7    80      0.410
